name: passive voice
title: Spanish Passive Voice Practice: Ser + Participle vs Passive Se
description: Practice the Spanish passive voice: ser + participle with por, the passive se, impersonal se and active alternatives, with a rule table and 10 checked sentences.
answer: Spanish has two passives. The true passive is ser + past participle, often with por: la casa fue construida por mi abuelo. The participle agrees with the subject. In everyday Spanish, the passive se is far more common when the doer does not matter: se venden casas, se habla español. Many English passives sound better as active sentences in Spanish.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.example: Las cartas fueron escritas por Ana.

rules.use: Passive se: verb agrees with the thing
rules.example: Se vende carro. Se venden carros.

quiz.why: The participle agrees with la novela: escrita.
Passive se agrees with the plural thing: se venden.
The doer in a passive: por.
A passive action in the future: ser, serán anunciados.

quiz.after: a los ganadores en la ceremonia.
quiz.why: With people introduced by a, se takes a singular verb: se premió a los ganadores.
Impersonal se with no object: singular, se cena.

mistakes: Overusing ser + participle: «el libro fue leído por mí» is correct but unnatural; «leí el libro» is better.
Not agreeing the participle: «las casas fueron construido» should be «construidas».
Using a singular verb with a plural thing in the passive se: «se vende casas» is common in signs, but the standard is «se venden casas».
Confusing ser and estar + participle: «la tienda es cerrada a las nueve» (action) and «la tienda está cerrada» (state).
Using de instead of por for the doer: «escrito de Cervantes» should be «escrito por Cervantes».

heritage: Heritage speakers in the US sometimes copy the English passive («fue dicho que…»), which sounds translated. Spanish usually prefers the passive se or an active sentence: «se dijo que…» or «dijeron que…». On signs, «se vende casas» is very common; writing expects «se venden casas».
teacher: Give students sentences from news headlines in English and ask them to translate with se or with an active verb, then compare which Spanish versions sound most natural.

faq.question: How do you form the passive voice in Spanish?
faq.answer: Ser in any tense + past participle + por + the doer: la carta fue escrita por Ana. The participle agrees with the subject in gender and number.

faq.question: What is the passive se?
faq.answer: Se + a third-person verb that agrees with the thing: se vende una casa, se venden casas. It is the usual Spanish choice when the doer is unknown or unimportant, much more common than ser + participle.

faq.question: Is the passive voice common in Spanish?
faq.answer: Ser + participle appears in news, history and formal writing, but everyday Spanish prefers the passive se or an active sentence. If an English passive sounds stiff in Spanish, make it active.
